subject.title: feat: centralized filename encoding utility for multi-encoding Content-Disposition handling

question: Where should the shared multi-encoding filename decoder live, and should https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/71517 be refreshed or replaced?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the permanent boundary affects core media, bundled channel plugins, and possible plugin-facing reuse; automation should not choose that API direction without maintainer intent.

options.title: Use media-core or a plugin-safe SDK boundary
options.body: Move the decoder into a reusable boundary and refresh the candidate PR or a replacement around that single shared helper.

options.title: Keep only narrow channel repairs for now
options.body: Treat the current Feishu fixes as sufficient until concrete non-Feishu encoding failures arrive.

options.title: Require broader live repros first
options.body: Keep the issue open but ask for real non-Feishu channel failures before approving a shared utility.

recommendation.title: Use media-core or a plugin-safe SDK boundary
recommendation.body: Move the decoder into a reusable boundary and refresh the candidate PR or a replacement around that single shared helper.

likelyOwner.reason: vincentkoc merged the two narrow Feishu filename fixes and is the strongest available routing owner for the media/channel boundary decision.
